newsitem.title: USA: J-Block ruling reversed in Enron's favor.
newsitem.headline: J-Block ruling reversed in Enron's favor.

text.p: Enron Corp said Thursday an English Court of Appeal has ruled in the company's favor, reversing a May 9 ruling in favor of the J-Block Sellers.

In the May ruling, the London court had ruled Enron could not refuse to agree to an early start date for its J-Block North Sea natural gas contract unless it had operation and technical reasons for deferring, the company explained.
The rulings are the latest in a long-running legal battle between Judy/Joanne (J-block) operator Phillips Petroleum Co and Enron, sparked by a slump in U.K. spot natural gas prices.

Phillips officials in Bartlesville, Okla., are preparing a statement on the appeal ruling, a spokeswoman said. In London, a Phillips company spokesman said the company will be applying to the UK House of Lords for leave to appeal the decision.

Enron said the "ruling means the start date under the contract, assuming the contract is not terminated, would be October 1, 1996. Take-or-pay payments, if any, would not fall due until the fourth quarter of 1997."
Phillips has a a 36.5 percent J-Block stake, while Agip SpA has 33 percent and British Gas Plc 30.5 percent.

Enron also said it is litigating in the London High Court starting October 28 as to whether the natural gas sale agreements are terminated due to the CATS parties' failure to have the required transportation facilities available by the deadline set forth in the Capacity Reservation and Transporation Agreement.
